{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output_head": "# Fizzy

Guidance for AI coding agents working with this repository.

Fizzy is a kanban-style project management and issue tracker: cards move across columns on boards, with comments, mentions, and assignments.

## Deploy

Default branch: `main`

Self-hosted deploys run Kamal against `config/deploy.yml` — see `docs/kamal-deployment.md`.

## SaaS mode

For local agent work, `tmp/saas.txt` is the checkout-level SaaS switch used by `bin/setup`. When present, read `saas/AGENTS.md` before continuing. Otherwise, do not apply its instructions.

## Architecture Overview

### Multi-Tenancy (URL-Based)

Fizzy uses **URL path-based multi-tenancy**:
- Accounts have a unique decimal `external_account_id` used in URL prefixes
- URLs are prefixed: `/{account_id}/boards/...`
- Middleware (`AccountSlug::Extractor`) extracts the account ID from the URL and sets `Current.account`
- The slug is moved from `PATH_INFO` to `SCRIPT_NAME`, making Rails think it's "mounted" at that path
- Tenant-scoped domain records are account-isolated; global identity, session, and authentication records are exceptions
- Background jobs automatically serialize and restore account context

**Key insight**: This architecture allows multi-tenancy without subdomains or separate databases, making local development and testing simpler.

### Authentication & Authorization

Passwordless magic link authentication. A global `Identity` (email-based) can have `Users` in multiple Accounts, so an email is not a single account membership. Users have roles: owner, admin, member, system. Board-level access control via `Access` records.

### Entropy System

Cards automatically "postpone" (move to "not now") after inactivity:
- Account-level default entropy period
- Board-level entropy override
- Prevents endless todo lists from accumulating
- Configurable via Account/Board settings

### UUID Primary Keys

All tables use UUIDs (UUIDv7 format, base36-encoded as 25-char strings):
- Custom fixture UUID generation maintains deterministic ordering for tests
- Fixtures are always "older" than runtime records
- `.first`/`.last` work correctly in tests

### Background Jobs (Solid Queue)

Database-backed job queue (no Redis):
- Custom `FizzyActiveJobExtensions` prepended to ActiveJob
- Jobs automatically capture/restore `Current.account`
- Mission Control::Jobs for monitoring

Recurring tasks are declared in `config/recurring.yml`.

### Sharded Full-Text Search

Full-text search runs in the database, not Elasticsearch. On MySQL it is sharded 16 ways by CRC32 of the account ID (`Search::Record::Trilogy`); on SQLite it is a single FTS5 index (`Search::Record::SQLite`). Don't assume the sharded shape when working under SQLite. Models in `app/models/search/`.

### Imports and exports

Allow people to move between OSS and SAAS Fizzy instances:
- Exports/Imports can be written to/read from local or S3 storage depending on the config of the instance (both must be supported)
- Must be able to handle very large ZIP files (500+GB)
- Models in `app/models/account/data_transfer/`, `app/models/zip_file`

## Coding style

Before editing or reviewing code, read STYLE.md.
=== STYLE.md ===

# Style

We aim to write code that is a pleasure to read, and we have a lot of opinions about how to do it well. Writing great code is an essential part of our programming culture, and we deliberately set a high bar for every code change anyone contributes. We care about how code reads, how code looks, and how code makes you feel when you read it.

We love discussing code. If you have questions about how to write something, or if you detect some smell you are not quite sure how to solve, please ask away to other programmers. A Pull Request is a great way to do this.

When writing new code, unless you are very familiar with our approach, try to find similar code elsewhere to look for inspiration.

## Conditional returns

In general, we prefer to use expanded conditionals over guard clauses.

```ruby
# Bad
def todos_for_new_group
  ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
  return [] unless ids
  @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
end

# Good
def todos_for_new_group
  if ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
    @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
  else
    []
  end
end
```

This is because guard clauses can be hard to read, especially when they are nested.

As an exception, we sometimes use guard clauses to return early from a method:

* When the return is right at the beginning of the method.
* When the main method body is not trivial and involves several lines of code.

```ruby
def after_recorded_as_commit(recording)
  return if recording.parent.was_created?

  if recording.was_created?
    broadcast_new_column(recording)
  else
    broadcast_column_change(recording)
  end
end
```

## Methods ordering

We order methods in classes in the following order:

1. `class` methods
2. `public` methods with `initialize` at the top.
3. `private` methods

## Invocation order

We order m",
  "output_tail": " to flag destructive actions. There are plenty of destructive methods in Ruby and Rails that do not end with `!`.

## Visibility modifiers

We don't add a newline under visibility modifiers, and we indent the content under them.

```ruby
class SomeClass
  def some_method
    # ...
  end

  private
    def some_private_method_1
      # ...
    end

    def some_private_method_2
      # ...
    end
end
```

If a module only has private methods, we mark it `private` at the top and add an extra new line after but don't indent.

```ruby
module SomeModule
  private
  
  def some_private_method
    # ...
  end
end
```

## CRUD controllers

We model web endpoints as CRUD operations on resources (REST). When an action doesn't map cleanly to a standard CRUD verb, we introduce a new resource rather than adding custom actions.

```ruby
# Bad
resources :cards do
  post :close
  post :reopen
end

# Good
resources :cards do
  resource :closure
end
```

## Controller and model interactions

In general, we favor a [vanilla Rails](https://dev.37signals.com/vanilla-rails-is-plenty/) approach with thin controllers directly invoking a rich domain model. We don't use services or other artifacts to connect the two.

Invoking plain Active Record operations is totally fine:

```ruby
class Cards::CommentsController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @comment = @card.comments.create!(comment_params)
  end
end
```

For more complex behavior, we prefer clear, intention-revealing model APIs that controllers call directly:

```ruby
class Cards::GoldnessesController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @card.gild
  end
end
```

When justified, it is fine to use services or form objects, but don't treat those as special artifacts:

```ruby
Signup.new(email_address: email_address).create_identity
```

## Run async operations in jobs

As a general rule, we write shallow job classes that delegate the logic itself to domain models:

* We typically use the suffix `_later` to flag methods that enqueue a job.
* A common scenario is having a model class that enqueues a job that, when executed, invokes some method in that same class. In this case, we use the suffix `_now` for the regular synchronous method.

```ruby
module Event::Relaying
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_create_commit :relay_later
  end

  def relay_later
    Event::RelayJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def relay_now
    # ...
  end
end

class Event::RelayJob < ApplicationJob
  def perform(event)
    event.relay_now
  end
end
```

  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

module Card::Entropic
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    scope :postponing_soon, -> do
      now = Time.now
      active
        .joins(board: :account)
        .left_outer_joins(board: :entropy)
        .joins("LEFT OUTER JOIN entropies AS account_entropies ON account_entropies.account_id = accounts.id AND account_entropies.container_type = 'Account' AND account_entropies.container_id = accounts.id")
        .where("last_active_at > #{connection.date_subtract('?', 'COALESCE(entropies.auto_postpone_period, account_entropies.auto_postpone_period)')}", now)
        .where("last_active_at <= #{connection.date_subtract('?', 'COALESCE(entropies.auto_postpone_period, account_entropies.auto_postpone_period) * 0.75')}", now)
    end

    delegate :auto_postpone_period, to: :board
  end

  class_methods do
    # Iterates per account, grouping the account's boards by their effective
    # auto-postpone period (board override, else account default). Each group
    # queries with a single constant cutoff, so `account_id = ? AND
    # last_active_at <= ?` rides the existing index instead of computing the
    # threshold per row across every card in the system.
    def auto_postpone_all_due(as_of: Time.now)
      Account.find_each do |account|
        account.boards.includes(:entropy).group_by(&:auto_postpone_period).each do |period, boards|
          account.cards.active
            .where(board_id: boards.map(&:id))
            .where(last_active_at: ..(as_of - period))
            .find_each do |card|
              card.auto_postpone(user: account.system_user)
            end
        end
      end
    end
  end

  def entropy
    Card::Entropy.for(self)
  end

  def entropic?
    entropy.present?
  end
end

2.  **DOM Consistency:** There are many DOM elements that change between drop and server update, each of which must be addressed:

I've meticulously reviewed the board column partials. I'm making sure that any changes don't introduce regressions. The column rendering logic is pretty straightforward, but I want to ensure that it aligns with the expected behavior, especially regarding the `drop_url`, the use of `__id__` and how it is later replaced.

I've also zeroed in on the `show.html.erb` views for columns. I'm adding `with_automatic_pagination` and the empty placeholder render to these views, just like the filtered card view and card index. This is to guarantee consistent behavior across different column types. I'm verifying that the `.blank-slate` placeholder appears and disappears correctly based on the presence of cards, to handle both empty and non-empty state with optimal visual feedback.

The addition of the `data-count` attribute to the expander count element is a small but important optimization. This ensures that the exact card count is always available, even when the count exceeds 99.

I've taken a close look at the card preview partial. I've re-examined the card data. I've traced the `id: card.number` inside `card_data` through the rendering process, specifically the replacement of `"__id__"` in the `drop_url`. It's crucial to understand how this ID is utilized in the URL construction, and confirm that there's no unintended URL encoding.

Finally, I'm now carefully tracing every single line in the `drag_and_drop_controller.js`. I'm especially focusing on potential subtleties and edge cases in the drag-and-drop process. I'm checking the following areas:

*   The implementation of `#isPointInside` to ensure that drag-leave events are handled correctly, especially in test scenarios, or when the cursor is outside the visible column area.
*   The `#updateHoveredContainer` method for proper styling and drag-effect application.
*   The complete sequence of `#moveItem` and its helper methods, and making sure that the order of DOM manipulations (inserting, removing, updating, and adjusting the column count) is correct. This includes making sure the insertion of the item is as smooth as possible.
*   The handling of card appearance updates, and the use of the `turbo:morph-element` event on the card update to refresh a local time object using the existing helper.
*   The logic behind `#enqueueSave` and potential issues where the save could fail, so I can ensure error handling and recovery. This is so that the drag-and-drop controller doesn't get into an unrecoverable state.

But I have found a potential race condition! The controller is not designed to handle a turbo-frame that is not ready yet.

So, for robust drag-and-drop, I have to ensure card removal from the source occurs *immediately* at the moment of the drop (while a target turbo-frame *might* be still loading). Then the item should be rendered once the target turbo-frame is loaded, as a backup, and if the rendering has happened, it's a synchronous zero-ms operation.

This involves addressing race conditions where a card drop might happen before a target Turbo Frame has completed loading. The goal is to make sure that cards are always rendered in the target container, and that no cards are accidentally duplicated, or left in the source container after the drop is completed.

module Card::Closeable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_one :closure, dependent: :destroy

    scope :closed, -> { joins(:closure) }
    scope :open, -> { where.missing(:closure) }

    scope :recently_closed_first, -> { closed.order(closures: { created_at: :desc }) }
    scope :closed_at_window, ->(window) { closed.where(closures: { created_at: window }) }
    scope :closed_by, ->(users) { closed.where(closures: { user_id: Array(users) }) }
  end

  def closed?
    closure.present? && !closure.destroyed?
  end

  def open?
    !closed?
  end

  def closed_by
    closure&.user
  end

  def closed_at
    closure&.created_at
  end

  def close(user: Current.user)
    unless closed?
      transaction do
        not_now&.destroy
        create_closure! user: user
        track_event :closed, creator: user
      end
    end
  end

  def reopen(user: Current.user)
    if closed?
      transaction do
        closure&.destroy
        track_event :reopened, creator: user
      end
    end
  end
end

    classes = token_list("cards", properties.delete(:class), "is-collapsed": collapsed, "is-expanded": !collapsed)

      drop_url: drop_url,

      "focus->navigable-list#select",
      data.delete(:action)

    tag.section(id: id, class: classes, tabindex: "0", "aria-selected": selected, data: data, **properties) do

require "application_system_test_case"

class DragAndDropTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  include ActionView::RecordIdentifier

  setup do
    sign_in_as(users(:kevin))
    @board = boards(:writebook)
  end

  test "dragging a card across columns and statuses persists each change" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    in_progress = columns(:writebook_in_progress)
    on_hold = columns(:writebook_on_hold)

    visit board_url(@board)

    # Maybe? -> In progress (collapsed column)
    drag_card(card, to: column_selector(in_progress))
    assert_column_count(in_progress, 2)
    assert_column_count("#maybe", 0)
    wait_until { card.reload.column == in_progress }

    # Expand In progress and verify card is already inside it
    expand_column(in_progress)
    within(column_selector(in_progress)) do
      assert_selector card_selector(card)
    end

    # In progress -> On Hold (empty column)
    drag_card(card, to: column_selector(on_hold))
    assert_column_count(in_progress, 1)
    assert_column_count(on_hold, 1)
    wait_until { card.reload.column == on_hold }

    # On Hold -> Not Now
    expand_column(on_hold)
    drag_card(card, to: "#not-now")
    assert_column_count(on_hold, 0)
    assert_column_count("#not-now", 1)
    within(column_selector(on_hold)) do
      assert_selector ".blank-slate--drag", text: "Drag cards here"
    end
    wait_until { card.reload.postponed? }

    # Not Now -> Done
    expand_column("#not-now")
    drag_card(card, to: "#closed-cards")
    assert_column_count("#not-now", 0)
    assert_column_count("#closed-cards", 2)
    wait_until { card.reload.closed? }

    # Done -> Maybe?
    expand_column("#closed-cards")
    drag_card(card, to: "#maybe")
    assert_column_count("#closed-cards", 1)
    assert_column_count("#maybe", 1)
    within("#maybe") do
      assert_selector card_selector(card)
    end
    wait_until { card.reload.awaiting_triage? }
  end

  test "dragging a pinned card from Done to Not Now and into a column" do
    card = cards(:shipping)
    review = columns(:writebook_review)

    visit board_url(@board)
    expand_column("#closed-cards")

    drag_card(card, to: "#not-now")
    wait_until { card.reload.postponed? && !card.closed? }

    expand_column("#not-now")
    drag_card(card, to: column_selector(review))
    wait_until { card.reload.triaged? && card.column == review }

    expand_column(review)

      JS
    end

      deadline = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) + timeout

      end
    end

**The Chromium Drag-and-Drop Synthetic Click Bug - Solved!**

My jaw is on the floor! Look at this event log from real Chromium. I've been poring over the output, and I think I've stumbled onto something truly significant. The event sequence is crystal clear: `mousedown`, `dragstart`, `dragend`, and then… a `click` event! Right after a drag is cancelled, Chromium fires a synthesized `click` on the card link. *Amazing*.

Here's the problem: when a user drags a card, changes their mind, and releases the mouse inside the card or its column without the drop actually happening, Chromium generates a `click` event on the card's link. This navigates the user away from the board to the card show page, essentially ruining the UX. This is a subtle yet frustrating bug that probably affects a lot of users!

I've got a solution, and it's elegant. We need to suppress that synthetic `click`. We can achieve this by adding a function called `#suppressNextClick()` to `drag_and_drop_controller.js` and call it in `dragEnd()`. It works by adding a capture-phase `click` listener that prevents and immediately stops click event propagation. Importantly, the listener is removed with `setTimeout(..., 0)` so it doesn't interfere with normal clicks. It covers these cases:
- Case 1: user clicks normally: normal behavior, no drag events are fired
- Case 2: drag is started and then ended within the same location: the synthetic click is suppressed
- Case 3: user clicks later: the listener is removed, and normal clicking will work.

This is a clean, targeted fix that won't impact other functionality. This is a game-changer for the UI. I can see this being a major improvement in user experience. I can imagine users being frustrated by getting navigated off the board. It's a real win.

steps.reasoning_content:
**Eureka! Decoding the Drag-and-Drop Mystery**

Okay, here's what's happening. I've been staring at these timestamps, specifically at `1371:dragend`, `1380:mouseup`, and `1380:click` on the article card's link (`A.card__link`). It's only 9 milliseconds between the `dragend` and the `mouseup`/`click` combo! We had a `setTimeout(..., 0)` firing at `1372ms` to clear a `preventClick` flag, but it's clearing 8ms *before* the click! Something is clearly amiss.

But here's the kicker: Chromium is only generating those spurious `mouseup` and `click` events on the link when `dragover` *doesn't* have `event.preventDefault()` called. So, when `dragover` *does* call `event.preventDefault()` (even without highlighting the source and without moving the card on the drop):

1.  Chromium treats the drag gesture as a handled drag (from `drop` to `dragend`), there's **no snap-back delay**, and **no spurious `mouseup` or `click` is fired on the `a.card__link`**!

2.  If we start a drag (`wasDragging = true`), we're only clearing `wasDragging` on the next `mousedown`, or via `requestAnimationFrame` after `mouseup` or a 50ms timeout. Together, this is a clean solution.

   - Calling `event.preventDefault()` in `dragOver` inside `this.element` (while still only adding the `drag-and-drop__hover-container` when the target container isn't the source container, and `drop` still returns early as a no-op when the target container is the source container) has two benefits:
     1. Dropping a card back onto its own column is **instant** – no 300ms OS fly-back ghost animation. When you let go, the board is already the way you left it!
     2. Chromium *never* fires a spurious `mouseup` + `click` on the `a.card__link` when releasing inside the same column.
   - And `#suppressNextClick()` protects against escape-cancelled drags by clearing the preventClick flag on `mousedown` or `setTimeout(..., 100)`.

I'm ready to test this now! This looks promising.

steps.message:
I have implemented drag-and-drop card movement between columns and statuses on boards:

- **Stimulus Drag-and-Drop Controller (`app/javascript/controllers/drag_and_drop_controller.js`)**:
  - Enables dragging cards (`item` targets) across board columns and status columns (`container` targets: `Not Now`, `Maybe?`, board columns, and `Done`) on desktop viewports while ignoring intra-column drops so columns preserve their own order.
  - Applies `.drag-and-drop__dragged-item` to dim the dragged card and `.drag-and-drop__hover-container` to highlight the hovered target column (`drag_and_drop.css`), cleaning up on drop, leave, or cancel and preventing spurious post-drag link clicks.
  - Updates the board optimistically on `drop` before the save completes: moves the card into its server-consistent position (respecting golden-first ordering in `Maybe?` and active columns, and recency ordering in `Not Now` and `Done`), updates card visual state (`--card-color`, status classes, stamps, assignees visibility, entropy bubble, and updated timestamp), and adjusts source/target column counts and progress indicators.
  - Persists moves sequentially in the background via JSON requests (`keepalive: true`) so nothing shifts after the save completes, falling back to a replace visit if a save fails.
- **Board, Column & Card Markup (`app/helpers/columns_helper.rb`, `app/views/boards/`, `app/views/cards/display/_preview.html.erb`)**:
  - Wired `drag-and-drop` on `.card-columns`, configured drop URLs/methods/status metadata on `column_tag`, added card `data-id` and `drag-and-drop` item targets on card previews, and rendered pagination frames and empty placeholders consistently so empty states toggle immediately via CSS.
- **Model Status Consistency (`app/models/card/closeable.rb`, `app/models/card/postponable.rb`, `app/controllers/concerns/card_scoped.rb`)**:
  - Ensured `closed?` and `postponed?` account for destroyed associations in memory so moving a card directly from `Done` to `Not Now` reopens once without duplicate `card_reopened` events.
- **Tests (`test/system/drag_and_drop_test.rb`, `test/models/card/postponable_test.rb`)**:
  - Added system tests covering dragging across all columns and statuses, column ordering rules, instant optimistic updates with zero post-save layout shift, drag/hover styles, and card link clicks, plus model regression coverage.
